trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the direct train from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (€5.40, ~17 minutes), then make your way to Canal House Amsterdam to check in and drop off luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a self-guided walk along the Jordaan neighborhood and the Prinsengracht canal. Explore the charming streets, browse local markets, and soak in the iconic canal views — completely free and a perfect gentle introduction to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Leidseplein square to enjoy the lively atmosphere and street performers. Walk along the Herengracht 'Golden Bend' for beautiful canal house views at dusk. End the evening with a relaxed dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or sandwich at Schiphol Airport before or after landing (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Grab a broodje (Dutch sandwich) from a local bakery or Albert Heijn supermarket near Centraal Station (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Moeders restaurant or Café de Reiger in Jordaan for classic Dutch stamppot or bitterballen (~€12–16)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Buy an OV-chipkaart (public transport card) at Schiphol for €7.50 deposit — it will save money throughout the trip. Consider picking up a GVB day pass for €9.50 if you plan to use trams frequently.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Open from 09:00. Arrive early to beat crowds and explore the Netherlands' premier museum housing masterpieces by Rembrandt, Vermeer, and Van Gogh. Allow 2.5–3 hours. Book tickets online in advance to save time (€22.50 adult). The stunning garden outside is free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Rijksmuseum, walk 10 minutes to the Van Gogh Museum Experience — Discover the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works, including 'The Bedroom' and 'Sunflowers.' Book timed entry online in advance (€22). Museumplein lawn between the two museums is a great free spot to rest.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Albert Cuyp Market area (closes around 17:00 on Sundays — check seasonally) or explore De Pijp neighborhood. Grab a stroopwafel from a street vendor (~€2) as an evening snack. Enjoy a canal-side walk back toward the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Bakkerij Hartog or a local café near the hotel for fresh bread and coffee (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Grab a herring (haring) from a street stall near Museumplein or a falafel wrap (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Surinamese restaurant in De Pijp neighborhood such as Roopram Roti for delicious roti and curry (~€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Book both the Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum online at least a week in advance — they sell out quickly, especially on weekends. The I Amsterdam City Card (€65/24hr) can be worth it if visiting multiple paid museums in one day, but buying individual tickets is fine for this itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — Book the first available morning slot (opens 09:00). Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during World War II. This deeply moving and historically significant experience requires advance booking — tickets sell out weeks ahead (~€16). Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour — After the Anne Frank House, walk to a nearby canal boat departure point. Join a group canal boat tour (budget option ~€15–18 per person) to cruise Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring. Glide past 17th-century merchant houses and historic bridges. Many tours depart from near Centraal Station or Leidseplein.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Negen Straatjes (Nine Little Streets) — a charming grid of boutique shops and cafés between the main canals. Window shop, grab a coffee, and enjoy the evening canal atmosphere. This area is very walkable from the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Café Winkel 43 near the Noordermarkt for famous Dutch apple pie and coffee (~€7–9)
meals.lunch: Broodje Bert or a local sandwich shop near the Anne Frank House (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Pancakes! Amsterdam (Prinsengracht location) for traditional Dutch savory or sweet pancakes (~€10–14)

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House MUST be booked online in advance — walk-in tickets are extremely rare and the queue without tickets is very long. The canal boat tour can be booked same-day from kiosks near the departure points, but booking online saves a small amount. Bring a light jacket — canal breezes can be cool in May.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the free Begijnhof — a hidden medieval courtyard with historic houses and a chapel, tucked away in the city center (free entry). Afterward, explore the Amsterdam Museum area and walk through the Spui square. Then head to the Flower Market (Bloemenmarkt) on the Singel canal — free to browse, a colorful Amsterdam icon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take tram or walk to Vondelpark — Amsterdam's beloved city park, perfect for a budget afternoon. Rent a bike from MacBike or Orangebike (~€10–13/day) and cycle through the park and along the canal ring. Cycling is the most authentic Amsterdam experience and lets you cover more ground affordably.
day_by_day.evening: Cycle or walk to the NDSM Wharf area via a free ferry from behind Centraal Station for Amsterdam's creative arts scene and street art. Alternatively, explore the lively Leidseplein bar scene for budget drinks (happy hour deals available at many bars).

meals.breakfast: Albert Heijn supermarket for yogurt, fruit, and fresh bread — assemble your own breakfast (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Vondelpark! Buy supplies from a supermarket or the market (~€5–7 total)
meals.dinner: Foodhallen (indoor food market in Oud-West) — multiple stalls with dishes from €8–12, great variety and atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The free ferry behind Centraal Station to Amsterdam Noord runs 24/7 and is a great free activity. Bike rental is highly recommended for this day — cycling the canal ring is quintessentially Amsterdam. Lock your bike securely at all times and use both locks provided.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hermitage Amsterdam area (now Amstelhof) and walk along the Amstel River — a less touristy canal stretch with beautiful views. Explore the Jewish Historical Museum quarter and the Portuguese Synagogue exterior (free from outside). Browse the Waterlooplein flea market for souvenirs and vintage finds (free entry, open Mon–Sat).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to any favorite spots or canals for last photos. Visit the FOAM Photography Museum near Keizersgracht (~€14) if budget allows, or simply walk the full length of Keizersgracht canal — one of the most scenic in the city. Pack and prepare for departure, storing luggage at the hotel if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Jordaan neighborhood. Enjoy a final canal-side drink at a brown café (bruine kroeg) — these traditional Dutch pubs are cozy and affordable. Head to Centraal Station for onward travel or airport transfer (train to Schiphol ~17 min, €5.40).

meals.breakfast: Café Brecht or local bakery near the hotel for a final Dutch breakfast (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: Dutch kroket or frikandel from a FEBO automat (iconic fast food wall) — a true local experience (~€2–4)
meals.dinner: De Bloemers or Café 't Smalle in Jordaan for a classic Dutch meal or bitterballen platter with drinks (~€12–16)

day_by_day.notes: Waterlooplein flea market is closed on Sundays — Tuesday through Saturday is ideal. Keep your OV-chipkaart for the airport train; check out at the yellow card reader to avoid extra charges. Amsterdam Centraal to Schiphol trains run every 10–15 minutes. Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for check-in and security.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the direct train from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (±17 min, ~€5). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely self-guided walk along the Herengracht and Prinsengracht canals near the hotel. Get oriented with the neighborhood, browse local boutiques, and soak in the iconic canal-house architecture. Stop by a nearby Albert Heijn or local bakery for a light snack.
day_by_day.evening: Private Canal Boat Tour — book an early-evening group canal cruise (departures typically run until 21:00) to see Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring beautifully lit as dusk falls. Glide past 17th-century merchant houses, drawbridges, and houseboats for a magical first-night introduction to the city.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a coffee and stroopwafel at Schiphol Airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Broodje Bert or a local eetcafé near Amsterdam Centraal for a classic Dutch broodje (sandwich) and soup — budget ~€10–14.
meals.dinner: Café Restaurant Amsterdam (Watertorenplein) — a grand Art Deco brasserie serving Dutch-French cuisine in a stunning converted pumping station. Mains ~€18–26.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 45–60 minutes for the Schiphol-to-hotel journey including the train and a short walk or taxi. Book the canal boat tour in advance online to secure an evening slot. Comfortable walking shoes recommended from day one.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — arrive at opening (9:00) to beat the crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Netherlands' premier museum: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and the vast collection of Dutch Golden Age masterpieces. Pre-book timed entry tickets online (~€22.50 per adult).
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience — located just steps from the Rijksmuseum on Museumplein, head straight there after lunch. Discover the world's largest Van Gogh collection including 'The Bedroom,' 'Sunflowers,' and self-portraits. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Tickets ~€22 — pre-book essential.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the lively Leidseplein square and surrounding streets. Enjoy the street performers and café terraces. Wind down with a Dutch beer at a traditional 'brown café' (bruine kroeg).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or nearby Scandinavian Embassy café for specialty coffee and avocado toast (~€10–14).
meals.lunch: Loetje aan het Museumplein — a beloved Amsterdam institution for Dutch beef sandwiches and salads, conveniently between the two museums. ~€14–18.
meals.dinner: Brasserie Keyzer (next to Concertgebouw) — a classic Amsterdam brasserie with Dutch and French dishes, open since 1905. Mains ~€20–28.

day_by_day.notes: Museum Square (Museumplein) is a 20–25 minute walk or short tram ride (Tram 2 or 12) from Canal House Amsterdam. Booking both museum tickets well in advance is strongly advised, especially for weekends in May. Consider purchasing an I Amsterdam City Card for unlimited public transport and museum discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — one of Amsterdam's most emotionally significant sites. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. Tickets must be booked online weeks in advance (~€16); entry slots fill up extremely fast. Allow 1.5 hours. The house is a short walk from Canal House Amsterdam along the Prinsengracht.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk — after the sobering morning, explore the charming Jordaan district directly adjacent to the Anne Frank House. Wander narrow streets lined with independent galleries, vintage shops, and flower-draped bridges. Visit the Noordermarkt area and browse local specialty food stalls and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Nine Streets (De 9 Straatjes) — a grid of boutique-filled streets connecting the main canals. Window shop, pick up souvenirs, and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere as the city quiets down on a Monday evening.

meals.breakfast: Winkel 43 in the Jordaan — famous for their apple pie, but also serves excellent breakfast. Arrive early to beat queues. ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Grab a herring (haring) from a street cart (a true Amsterdam experience, ~€4) plus a Dutch cheese sandwich from Kaasland on the Noordermarkt. Total ~€10.
meals.dinner: De Reiger in the Jordaan — a cozy, authentic Dutch eetcafé with a rotating seasonal menu and excellent local beers. Mains ~€16–24. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House is extremely popular — tickets often sell out 6–8 weeks ahead. If tickets are unavailable, consider the nearby Jewish Historical Museum or the Dutch Resistance Museum as meaningful alternatives. The Jordaan and Nine Streets are entirely walkable from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Foam Photography Museum or the Amsterdam Museum (Amsterdams Historisch Museum) for a deeper cultural dive. Alternatively, explore the Begijnhof — a hidden medieval courtyard garden tucked in the city center, free to enter and remarkably peaceful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided cycling tour of Amsterdam's outer canal ring (Singelgracht). Rent a bike from MacBike or Orangebike (~€14/day) and cycle along the quieter eastern canals: Keizersgracht, Reguliersgracht, and the famous 'seven bridges' viewpoint on Reguliersgracht. Extend the ride to the vibrant De Pijp neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore De Pijp neighborhood — Amsterdam's bohemian quarter. Browse the Albert Cuyp Market (open until 17:30), then relax at one of the many lively café terraces along Ferdinand Bolstraat as the evening begins.

meals.breakfast: Bakers & Roasters in De Pijp — a popular brunch spot with New Zealand-inspired dishes and excellent coffee. ~€12–16.
meals.lunch: Albert Cuyp Market street food — try fresh stroopwafels, poffertjes (mini pancakes), and Dutch fries (patat) with satay sauce. ~€8–12 total.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Baut — a stylish mid-range restaurant in De Pijp serving modern European cuisine with a strong focus on seasonal Dutch produce. Mains ~€20–28. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: May weather in Amsterdam can be unpredictable — pack a light rain jacket for cycling. Bike lanes are extensive and well-marked, but traffic can be busy; stay alert at intersections. The Albert Cuyp Market is closed on Sundays, so Tuesday is a great day to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit the Bloemenmarkt (Floating Flower Market) on the Singel canal, the world's only floating flower market. Browse tulip bulbs, Dutch souvenirs, and fresh blooms. Then walk through the charming Spui square and browse the Friday book market stalls (note: Spui book market runs on Fridays — on Wednesday explore nearby Athenaeum Boekhandel bookshop instead).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration: revisit a favorite canal-side spot, do any remaining shopping along Kalverstraat or PC Hooftstraat, or relax at a canal-side café with a final Dutch coffee and apple pie. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparation — depending on your outbound flight time, take the train from Amsterdam Centraal to Schiphol (±17 min). Enjoy a final Dutch beer or bitterbal (deep-fried snack) at a Centraal Station café before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Brecht — a cozy, literary-themed café near Rembrandtplein serving excellent coffee and pastries. ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Brouwerij 't IJ — Amsterdam's iconic windmill brewery for a final Dutch craft beer paired with a cheese platter or bitterballen. ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Early dinner (if departing late) at Moeders ('Mothers') restaurant — a beloved Amsterdam institution with home-style Dutch cooking, walls covered in family photos, and a warm, nostalgic atmosphere. Mains ~€16–22. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (typically 11:00–12:00) and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon activities. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the journey to Schiphol and airport security. Tulip bulbs purchased at the Bloemenmarkt are certified for import to most countries — check your destination's customs rules before buying.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Schiphol to Canal House Amsterdam via chauffeured Mercedes-Benz E-Class. Check-in, settle into your canal-view suite, and refresh after the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour: After settling in, step directly onto a private canal boat departing near your hotel. Glide through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring, passing 17th-century merchant houses, hidden gardens, and iconic drawbridges. Your private guide will narrate the Golden Age history of the city. Duration approximately 2 hours — the perfect, leisurely introduction to Amsterdam without overwhelming yourself on arrival day.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Herengracht and Keizersgracht canals at dusk as the city lights begin to reflect off the water. Enjoy a pre-dinner aperitif at the hotel's intimate bar before heading out for a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival. Light welcome amenity (champagne, Dutch cheeses, and seasonal fruit) prepared in your suite by Canal House Amsterdam upon check-in.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick but quality bite near the hotel at Café Papeneiland — one of Amsterdam's oldest brown cafés, serving classic Dutch uitsmijter (open-faced egg and ham sandwich) and fresh stroopwafels in a cozy, historic setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vinkeles (inside The Dylan Amsterdam, a 5-minute canal-side walk) — a Michelin-starred restaurant set within an 18th-century bakery. Indulge in the multi-course tasting menu featuring modern French-Dutch cuisine with an exceptional wine pairing. Reservations essential; book in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Given the 13:00 arrival, immigration, baggage, and transfer will realistically place you at the hotel around 14:30–15:00. The Private Canal Boat Tour is ideal as a first activity — relaxing, scenic, and requires no walking. Request your hotel concierge to pre-arrange the private boat departure for 15:30. Vinkeles dinner reservation should be made well in advance given Michelin-star demand.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit: Begin your day at the Netherlands' premier museum, housing masterpieces by Rembrandt, Vermeer, and a vast collection of Dutch Golden Age art. Arrange a private guided tour (2–2.5 hours) through the highlights — including Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' and Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid' — bypassing general queues with a luxury skip-the-line experience. The museum's stunning Gothic-Renaissance architecture and manicured garden are equally impressive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience: Just a short walk from the Rijksmuseum in Museum Square, immerse yourself in the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works, including 'The Bedroom,' 'Sunflowers,' and hundreds of letters and sketches. Opt for a premium timed-entry slot and consider a private docent-led tour for deeper context into Van Gogh's turbulent life and revolutionary technique. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Take an evening walk along the illuminated Prinsengracht canal before dinner. After dinner, consider a nightcap at Pulitzer's Bar — a sophisticated, literary-themed bar inside the Pulitzer Amsterdam hotel, just steps from Canal House.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent breakfast at the Canal House Amsterdam's dining room — expect freshly baked breads, smoked salmon, Dutch cheeses, seasonal fruit, eggs to order, and fine coffee. Take your time; museums open at 09:00.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Rijksmuseum's own Grand Café Cobra or, for a premium option, walk five minutes to Brasserie Ambassade on the Herengracht — elegant French-Dutch brasserie fare with canal views, perfect between museum visits.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spectrum (inside Hotel de L'Europe) — a Michelin two-star restaurant offering an avant-garde tasting menu that celebrates Dutch ingredients with global technique. Exceptional wine cellar and impeccable service in a grand 19th-century setting on the Amstel River.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday mornings at both museums can be busy — luxury pre-booked skip-the-line entry and private guides are strongly recommended. Museum Square (Museumplein) connects both museums with a pleasant 5-minute walk. Wear comfortable shoes for the day. The hotel concierge can arrange all museum bookings and private guide coordination.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour: One of Amsterdam's most profoundly moving experiences. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid for over two years during the Nazi occupation. A deeply emotional and historically significant visit. Sunday morning slots sell out weeks in advance — ensure your luxury concierge has secured a timed-entry ticket. Allow approximately 1.5 hours. The house is a short, picturesque walk along the Prinsengracht from your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk: Transition from reflection to discovery with a guided walk through Amsterdam's most charming neighborhood. Meander through narrow streets, cross quaint bridges, and explore hidden courtyards (hofjes). Stop at the famous Albert Cuyp Market (a 15-minute tram ride away) for artisan Dutch treats — fresh stroopwafels, raw herring, and aged Gouda. Return through the Jordaan's gallery-lined streets and boutique shops. A private food and culture guide will elevate the experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset canal cruise: Board a private electric boat for a golden-hour cruise through the smaller, less-touristed canals of the Jordaan and Western Canal Ring. Many operators offer on-board wine and cheese service — the perfect way to end a full day. Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel. Alternatively, walk to Greenwoods on the Singel — a beloved Amsterdam institution serving generous English-style breakfasts with excellent coffee in a cozy canal-house setting.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Breda in the Jordaan — a celebrated Dutch restaurant with a focus on seasonal, locally sourced ingredients. Their weekend lunch menu is elegant yet relaxed, with natural wines and creative small plates.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ciel Bleu (Hotel Okura, 23rd floor) — a Michelin two-star restaurant with panoramic views over Amsterdam's skyline and canals. French-influenced fine dining with an exceptional sake and wine program. A truly spectacular setting for a Sunday evening.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House does not allow large bags — leave luggage at the hotel or use the cloakroom. Photography is not permitted inside the annex. The Jordaan walk pairs beautifully with the morning's reflective mood, offering a gradual shift to Amsterdam's vibrant, artistic street life. The evening electric boat cruise can be arranged through the hotel concierge — request a bottle of Ruinart Blanc de Blancs on board.

day_by_day.morning: Private Art Gallery and Antique Market Tour: Explore Amsterdam's thriving art scene beyond the major museums. Visit the Foam Photography Museum on the Keizersgracht for world-class contemporary photography exhibitions. Then browse the Spiegelkwartier — Amsterdam's prestigious antique district — with a private art advisor who can guide you through rare Dutch Golden Age prints, Delftware, and contemporary Dutch art. A unique opportunity for discerning collectors or simply curious luxury travelers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Heineken Experience or Distillery Tour (premium option): For a more indulgent afternoon, arrange a private tour of the Wynand Fockink distillery (est. 1679) — one of Amsterdam's oldest jenever (Dutch gin) distilleries, tucked in a hidden alley behind the Royal Palace. Enjoy a guided tasting of aged jenevers and liqueurs in their intimate tasting room. Alternatively, explore the Royal Palace on Dam Square and the surrounding historic city center on foot with a private historian guide.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical concert at the Concertgebouw — one of the world's finest concert halls with near-perfect acoustics. Check the May 2027 program in advance; the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra frequently performs on Monday evenings. A pre-concert dinner nearby makes for a perfectly cultured evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel. Request a room service option if you prefer a slow, private morning with canal views from your suite.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café de Jaren — a grand, airy café on the Amstel River with a beautiful waterside terrace. Known for its fresh salads, Dutch open sandwiches, and excellent coffee. A beloved local institution with a relaxed, sophisticated atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Le Garage — a theatrical, beloved Amsterdam brasserie frequented by artists, musicians, and the city's creative elite. Bold French-Dutch cuisine, an eclectic interior, and a lively atmosphere. Book a table for 18:00 to allow time for the Concertgebouw.

day_by_day.notes: Concertgebouw tickets for popular programs sell out quickly — book as early as possible through their official website or via your hotel concierge. The Wynand Fockink distillery is a hidden gem that most tourists miss; the private tasting is an authentic, intimate Amsterdam experience. The Spiegelkwartier antique district is closed on Sundays, making Monday the ideal day to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Keukenhof Day Trip (if May tulip season is still active) or Amsterdam Forest Escape: If the famous Keukenhof Gardens are still in bloom (they typically close mid-May, so confirm 2027 dates), arrange a private chauffeured trip to Lisse (45 minutes from Amsterdam) to walk through 7 million tulips and spring flowers in one of the world's most spectacular garden displays. If Keukenhof has closed, opt instead for a private guided cycling tour through the Amsterdamse Bos (Amsterdam Forest) — a vast, peaceful green lung south of the city, offering a serene contrast to the urban canal experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Canal Stroll and Shopping: Return to Amsterdam for a leisurely final afternoon. Browse the luxury boutiques along the P.C. Hooftstraat (Amsterdam's premier luxury shopping street — home to Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Chanel, and local Dutch designers). Stop at Metz & Co or Coster Diamonds (near Museumplein) for a diamond polishing demonstration — Amsterdam has been the world's diamond capital since the 17th century. Return to the hotel for final packing and a farewell aperitif on your canal-view balcony.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and relaxed evening along the canals. Walk the illuminated Herengracht one final time after dinner, absorbing the timeless beauty of Amsterdam by night.

meals.breakfast: A special farewell breakfast at the hotel — request the full spread with Dutch specialties including fresh hagelslag (chocolate sprinkles on buttered bread), warm stroopwafels, smoked eel, and a glass of fresh orange juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch at De Kas — a legendary Amsterdam restaurant set inside a 1926 greenhouse in the Frankendael Park. Hyper-seasonal, garden-to-table cuisine where nearly everything on the menu is grown on-site or sourced within hours. A truly unique and memorable Amsterdam dining experience.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Rijks Restaurant (inside the Rijksmuseum) — a sophisticated restaurant offering modern Dutch cuisine inspired by the museum's Golden Age collection. Beautifully presented seasonal dishes, an outstanding Dutch wine and jenever program, and a stunning setting within one of the world's great cultural institutions. The perfect final evening in Amsterdam.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm Keukenhof's 2027 closing date well in advance — in some years it closes May 10th, in others May 18th or later. If unavailable, the cycling tour through Amsterdamse Bos is an equally premium, memorable alternative. Arrange departure logistics with the hotel concierge — a private chauffeured transfer back to Schiphol should be booked for your departure day. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before any international flight departure.
